title: RX: a mid-frame rx_err_i pulse is ignored and the frame dispatches
body:
[R1]

Found by the cleared-context review of PR #34 and measured at both `main@5d4fcc67` and that PR's head; PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by it, so it was filed rather than folded in.

## What is wrong

`rx_err_i` is documented as an abort that drops the frame silently, and the module header lists it among the DROP arms, but it is read only inside the end-of-frame branch (`hdl/wire/KL_gptp_rx_parser.sv:458`, reaching only `fin_ok_r`). A pulse anywhere before the last byte is therefore ignored and the frame dispatches normally.

## Measured

A 58-byte Sync, with `rx_err_i` raised for one byte at three positions, identical at base and at PR #34's head:

| error position | drops | events |
|---|---|---|
| byte 20 (mid-frame) | +0 | +1 |
| byte 40 (mid-frame) | +0 | +1 |
| byte 57 (the eof byte) | +1 | +0 |

So the abort works only when the flag happens to be held to the end of the frame.

## Impact

Bounded today, and that boundedness is worth stating precisely rather than assuming. In the parent integration the port is tied off: `hdl/ieee8021as/gptp_plane/KL_gptp_shadow.sv:447` drives `.rx_err_i (1'b0)` because the frame FIFO never delivers a bad frame, and the parent records that as a deliberate constant. So no shipping path reaches this today. It becomes live the moment anything drives the port from a MAC that flags the corrupt byte rather than holding the flag to eof, which is the common behaviour, and then a corrupted frame is parsed and dispatched as if clean.

## What to do

Either latch `rx_err_i` into `bad_r` on any byte, so an abort anywhere in the frame refuses it and counts one drop, or narrow the port documentation and the module header to say the signal is sampled only with the last byte and must be held there by the driver. The first is the safer default; the second is acceptable if the interface contract is genuinely "held to eof", in which case say so where an integrator will read it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The chosen contract is stated in the port documentation and the module header, and the code matches it.
- [ ] If latched: an `rx_err_i` pulse at any byte position refuses the frame with exactly one counted drop, no event and no bank write, tested at the first byte, mid-frame and the eof byte.
- [ ] A planted mutation restoring mid-frame acceptance goes red; README counts updated.
- [ ] `feed_gap` in the parser bench drives `rx_err_i` explicitly rather than relying on a neighbouring feeder leaving it low (noted in the same review).

Related: #27 (PR #34), #33, and the parent's tie-off at `KL_gptp_shadow.sv:447`.
